confidence_rationale: Direct ML analogue of MECH-343's core prediction: a state-conditioned exploration signal f(s) tied to uncertainty outperforms the constant-exploration instance f(s)=c and other fixed-schedule exploration methods (RND, UCB, NoisyNets) on hard MuJoCo tasks. Strongly relevant to the 'gated entropy > always-high entropy' half of Q-056. Held to 0.60 because the paper does NOT include a pure no-exploration arm (so the 'gated > OFF' half is untested here), the gating signal is generic uncertainty rather than REE's specific difficulty/stuck-state signal, and there is no goal/harm-constraint structure as in MECH-343.
failure_signatures: Constant exploration f(s)=c is an internal control that the adaptive (state-conditioned) variants beat -- evidence that always-on fixed exploration is dominated by conditional exploration.
Tested only on dense-reward MuJoCo; authors flag sparse-reward domains as untested, which is closer to REE's hard-goal/blocked-path regime.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A generic framework that conditions the exploration signal on a per-state uncertainty estimate f(s) yields adaptive exploration that outperforms a constant-exploration instance f(s)=c and standard fixed exploration methods (RND, UCB, Noisy Nets) across six hard MuJoCo tasks (15 runs each).
mapping.ree_translation: This is the ML evidence for MECH-343: making proposal entropy a function of state (here, uncertainty; in REE, stuck-state/difficulty) beats holding it constant. The f(s)=c control is the literature analogue of Q-056's 'always-high entropy' arm, and the adaptive variant is the analogue of the 'stuck-state-gated entropy' arm. Adaptive winning supports the prediction that conditional entropy dominates a fixed-high regime.
mapping.mapping_caveat: No pure-exploitation (entropy-OFF) baseline is reported, so the experiment evidences 'gated > constant-high' but NOT the full three-way 'gated > both off and always-high' discrimination that Q-056/EXP-0176 requires. The gating variable is generic epistemic uncertainty / model-disagreement, not REE's difficulty-or-stuck-state signal, and there is no goal-progress or harm constraint -- so commitment-latency and no-harm-increase predictions are out of scope here.
mapping.source_context: Deep RL (TD3 backbone), continuous-control MuJoCo robotics, dense reward; simulation.

confidence_components.notes: Peer-reviewed (AAMAS 2026 full paper) but a single methods paper, not a meta-analysis. Mapping fidelity moderate: covers gated-vs-constant but not gated-vs-off; transfer risk moderate (MuJoCo continuous control -> REE discrete arbitration).
